update.subtitle: from the Git repository
update.notARepo: This directory is not a Git repository, so the updater is inactive. It only runs on an installed server, from a clone under /opt. Nothing to do in a development setup.

update.confirm_other: Install the update now ({{count}} new commits)? The service pulls the new files and restarts.
update.inProgress: Update triggered. The service pulls the files, builds the frontend and restarts, which can take one or two minutes. The page reloads automatically once the server is back.
update.howItWorksBody: The backend never runs an update itself (it is unprivileged). It writes a trigger; a systemd .path unit picks that up and runs deploy/update.sh as the app user:
update.configNote: Configuration (.env): UPDATE_BRANCH. Untracked files (.env, backend/data/) are preserved.

search.noServiceAccount: AD search not possible: no LDAP service account is configured. Set bind user, bind password and base DN under "AD/LDAP".
search.packageMissing: AD search not possible: the "ldap3" package is missing on the server.
search.bindFailed: AD not reachable: the service account could not sign in ({{detail}}). Check the connection and credentials under "AD/LDAP".
search.searchFailed: AD rejected the search ({{detail}}). Check the base DN and the rights of the service account under "AD/LDAP".

users.groupCreated: Group created. Now assign rights and members.
users.accountsHint: Only local accounts (break glass) are listed here. Rights come from groups below, so an account without a group has no rights. AD users get no account: they are granted once as a member of a group (directly or through an AD group), and at sign-in their current AD membership counts.
users.adLoginsHint: No accounts, just whoever has already signed in over AD or SSO. Rights come from the groups; an entry here grants nothing and comes back by itself at the next sign-in.
users.groupsHint: A group grants rights (checkboxes) to its members: local accounts, single AD users or whole AD groups (everyone AD says is in them). A person's effective rights are the union of every group they belong to.
users.fullAccess: Full access: every right, including future ones
users.fullAccessNote: This group automatically holds every right, including rights from later versions. Without the switch a rights list ages: a newly added right would be missing and nobody could grant it, because you may only grant what you hold yourself.
users.wildcardPost: the text is matched anywhere in the name.

ldap.saved: Saved. Applied right away and kept across restarts.
ldap.subtitle: shared sign-in
ldap.intro: Active as soon as server, domain and base DN are set. Local accounts always stay valid as break glass. The mapping from AD groups to rights lives in the "{{accounts}}" tab.
ldap.serverHint: One or more DCs (comma separated): the first is primary, the rest are failover. Scheme per entry:
ldap.baseDnHint: Search base for the group lookup.
ldap.useSsl: LDAPS (TLS) for bare host names, a scheme prefix (gc://…) wins
ldap.bindUserHint: UPN or DN for the group search. Empty = the signing-in user binds.
ldap.footnotePost: (bootstrap and fallback only). The bind password is stored encrypted and never returned in clear text.

sso.saved: Saved. Applied right away and kept across restarts.
sso.subtitle: Entra ID (optional)
sso.intro1: An extra sign-in path over OIDC (authorization code + PKCE). Local accounts and the AD password login stay unchanged. Active as soon as Active is set and issuer, client ID and client secret are present.
sso.intro2: Groups are loaded live from AD or the global catalog, as with the AD login (service account under "{{ldap}}"), and mapped to rights in the "{{accounts}}" tab.
sso.enabled: SSO active (shows the "{{label}}" button on the sign-in page)
sso.issuerHint: Discovery base (…/.well-known/openid-configuration). Entra: insert the tenant ID.
sso.clientIdHint: Application (client) ID from the Entra app registration.
sso.redirectHint: Must be registered in the Entra app registration. Empty = derived from the request (better set explicitly behind a reverse proxy):
sso.scopesHint: openid is required; profile and email supply name and UPN.
sso.footnotePost: (bootstrap and fallback only). The client secret is stored encrypted and never returned in clear text. An SSO sign-in without a matching AD group gets no access.
